\subsubsection{Not Yet Verified}\label{sss:pixtop-open}

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item \textbf{Devices outside the statistics.} Of the 742 mismatch-capable
    device instances in the executed netlist, 587 carry mismatch, four have it
    explicitly switched off and 151 sit on raw model cards. No matched structure
    is excluded: the four are bias-rail decoupling capacitors, out by intent
    because they decouple rather than match, and the 151 are the converter's
    sample switch and level shifters, the multiplexer pass gates, the bias
    generator's start-up branch and the digital cells of the
    successive-approximation logic. Two structures were admitted after
    Table~\ref{tab:pixtop-mc} was measured, and neither moves it: capacitor
    mismatch is invisible to a dc campaign by construction, and the divider that
    sets the converter's threshold is isolated from the readout by the
    buffer. That divider is worth its own note --- with its matching disabled it
    reported a threshold of exactly \SI{1.250000}{\volt} in all 200 samples,
    because process cancels in a ratio of identical resistors and a matched pair
    switched off reads as an ideal reference rather than a disabled one. Enabled
    it carries \SI{0.968}{\milli\volt}, \num{0.607} of a converter code ---
    dormant while the array is unpopulated, and a converter offset as soon as a
    code is scored.
  \item \textbf{The converter at schematic level.} Its capacitor array exists
    only in the extracted view (Section~\ref{sss:pixtop-adc}), so the code the
    schematic tests report is stuck and is deliberately left unspecced.
  \item \textbf{Current read as a code.} No run has taken a real electrode
    current through the on-chip converter. The voltammogram of
    Section~\ref{sss:pixtop-cv} reads current from an in-line probe and from
    the measured transimpedance; the converter figures of
    Section~\ref{sss:pixtop-adc} come from known voltages applied at the
    multiplexer. The two have not been closed into one measurement.
  \item \textbf{Layout parasitics on the compensation node.} The
    \SI{10853}{\micro\meter\squared} of capacitor added by
    Section~\ref{sss:pixtop-stability} sits on the transimpedance summing node,
    the one node in the channel where stray capacitance costs phase margin. No
    stability or noise figure here carries its wiring parasitics: the stage has
    no extracted view.
  \item \textbf{Wiring.} All sixteen test-port multiplexer inputs are undriven,
    so the debug path selects between floating nodes on demand --- and its
    output now carries a buffer, which spends \SI{243}{\micro\watt} of
    Section~\ref{sss:pixtop-power} driving them. Either the inputs get something
    to look at or the buffer goes; as built it is the second-largest consumer in
    the channel. Eleven of the converter multiplexer's sixteen slots are
    undriven the same way, and one of them is the level-1 sibling of the
    commanded-potential output, so it injects its accumulated charge into that
    output on every toggle of the lowest select bit
    (Section~\ref{sss:pixtop-mux}). The fix is one wire per input, to the
    common mode rather than to local ground.
\end{itemize}
